rubric_notes: Correct 2.08 hierarchy with sunids, five families and TAF membership verified via children listings; fold a.22 single superfamily verified via children; a.22.1.2 lineage retrieved. Organizes relatives by how far down the hierarchy they share placement, states superfamily implies probable common ancestry but not identical function, and warns that histone-fold proteins differ in DNA binding, partner pairing and role. Honestly scopes what was not retrieved (lineages for name matches, per-domain annotations). Treats automated-matches bins correctly. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct sccs, family/superfamily/fold sunids, names and species. Superfamily correctly stated as the homology-bearing level versus fold as structural grouping; explicitly rejects reading family split as non-homology, rejects HisE/MazG transfer in both directions, templates, Li/UNL as ligand evidence, and notes no sequence/structure alignment was retrieved. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Superfamily 53067, fold 53066, families with sunids and the hexokinase upward trace (53084 parents) all supported by the bundle; separate Glucokinase family c.55.1.7 also supported. Correct divergent-homolog interpretation at superfamily level, conserved two-lobed a/b ATP-binding core, and explicit limits: no transferable function, substrate, reaction, mechanism or regulation, no interchangeable template; fold alone only structural similarity. All criteria met. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Correct hierarchy with SUNIDs, all supported by the bundle (Mn-catalase lineage, superfamily children). Interprets shared superfamily as probable common ancestry with family-level functional divergence, rejects both shared-function and unrelated-because-different-chemistry readings, states that catalase/RNR calls require active-site, ligand, sequence and experimental evidence, and distinguishes fold-level similarity from the superfamily claim. Notes what was not retrieved. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct families/sunids/fold/superfamily and representative domains d1iuza_, d1ikop_, d5n0ya1 with annotations (cu/so4; 8fq/ca/so4; automated match to d1wd8a2) and homology responses all supported. Correctly frames superfamily as remote homology, rejects function/template transfer, lists evidence required, and explicitly avoids calling them analogous. Minor: the statement that the ephrin record has no copper annotation is not backed by a d1ikop_ annotations call in its bundle, though it is accurate. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

All three families, superfamily, fold, class and sunids correct and bundle-supported; sf homology flag and empty warnings correctly cited. Clear remote-ancestry/scaffold interpretation, family as closer level, rejects conjugation, RBD->p97, UBX->Ras and template transfers. Bonus bundle-supported caution about name-only matches (c.47.1.24, a.5.2.1, a.4.1.1) and fold-vs-superfamily homology distinction; limits stated.

All classifications and sunids correct and supported (52172, 52171, 51349, 52173 with d1u0sy_ T. maritima, 52252, 82344 with d1r8ja2 2-135); annotation and homology responses correctly described; transparent about which lineages were retrieved. Reasoning: superfamily asserts probable common ancestry inferred from structure, more distant than within-family; explicitly rejects phospho-acceptor Asp/Mg2+/CheA/CheZ/motor transfer, catalytic or PLP-binding transfer, clock-function transfer, template interchangeability, and convergence/analogy claims; distinguishes fold/class similarity from superfamily homology; does not misplace ODC catalysis. No material issues. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Correct b.84.5/b.84.5.1 placement under fold b.84 with sunids, siblings, fold comment and PubMed all supported by bundle. Clearly distinguishes fold (architecture only, cites fold-level homology warning) from superfamily (probable ancestry within b.84.5 only), states family-level homology of V1/A1 bulge domains without extending to b.84.1-b.84.4, and explicitly says separate superfamilies do not show analogy or convergence. No function/template transfer. All must_include met; no must_avoid violated. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Fold, class and three superfamilies with sunids supported by the parents/children responses; the f.21.1 homology record (implied at sf scope) and f.21.1 comment on conserved heme ligands are in the bundle and correctly interpreted as within-superfamily evidence only. Calibrated: separate superfamilies are absence of an assertion, not proof of analogy; no function/ligand/template transfer; names sequence/structure alignment and literature as needed evidence and states what was not retrieved. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct identifiers and lineage supported by bundle; notes functional breadth of c.2.1. Reads superfamily as remote probable ancestry and family separation as substantial divergence in sequence, domain context and function. States superfamily membership does not establish function, substrate, reaction, mechanism or ligand specificity; different roles and partner domains for ADH C-terminal, CoA-binding and channel regulatory domains; refuses to transfer binding residues or use interchangeable templates; notes fold indicates only structural similarity. Slightly less explicit about what family-specific evidence to collect, but limits are clearly stated. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct lineage (k.40.1.1, family sunid 100905, protein/species sunids) and sensible designed-protein caveat that the shared family is not evidence of natural descent. However it never retrieved or mentions the family node's 'not a true family' comment, and its homology framing ('SCOPe's hierarchy implies homology between the two domains') rests on the generic level semantics the annotation overrides. Only domain-level endpoints were checked, so the 'no homology warnings' statement is incomplete. Decisive annotation ignored: bio ceiling 2; important annotation missing: factual 2.

Verified both releases: 1.69 d1t1ja_ c.137.1.1 novel singleton fold vs d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1; 2.08 d1t1ja1 c.23.14.2 sibling family to c.23.14.1 under shared c.23.14. Interprets the move as SCOPe asserting superfamily-level probable common ancestry (not family), notes retained sunids and split l-class artifacts, and gives function/template, rationale, and intermediate-release caveats.

Correct artifact identification (class l, Tags lineage, N-terminal Tags, Synthetic, l.1.1.1) and correct d1a14h1 b.1.1.1 VH lineage, all bundle-supported including Fab NC10 comment and homology responses for both segments. Rejects tag similarity as homology, notes same tag can appear on unrelated proteins, directs inference to the VH domain, and states limits. Complete.

Full 1.75 f.11.1.1 and 2.08 two-class split correct, with strong modules interpretation, correct superfamily/family/fold distinctions, and no unsafe whole-chain transfer. States only 1.75 and 2.08 were compared, so omits the 2.04 split pinpoint.

All five domains correctly identified with boundaries, sccs and lineage, all supported by the evidence bundle. Correctly states bromodomain is a family-level placement, the other three are Prp8-specific families in known superfamilies, and d.394 is the new Prp8-specific fold. Mosaic interpretation, group II intron link flagged as outside SCOPe, no function transfer, and no nonhomology claim between domains. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge, 2026-10-22.

All required content present: shared lineage, 're' flag, 'single repeat', 4cj9 A:259-292 representative and coordinate caveat. Minor loose phrasing ('superfamily-level homology') but conclusion is drawn at the family level. Good limits on RVD specificity and template use.

Correct metadata and periodic label 2.08-2026-08-16 (bundle-supported), with retrieval date. Cites stable 2.08 and pins release=2.08; periodic label as a dated qualifier in addition, never alone. States periodic is a dated interim layer that is not a new stable release and does not replace 2.08. Omits that periodic updates add newly classified PDB entries without rewriting stable domains. No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Correct a.47.2.1 placement, lineage, protein nodes, 'automated match to d3c98b_', fragment comment and 'ms' flag, all in the bundle; 3c98 obsoletion is true. Clearly argues the three-helix portion could alone suggest a generic spectrin/STAT-like bundle, that the complete 1dn1 B domain validates the family placement, and that fragments must not define topology, boundaries or templates. Correct homology semantics (homology_implied_by_level, fold not ancestry, spectrin comment not homology), no function transfer, honest about unverified history and absent quality data.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Verified c.2.1/c.2 and c.3.1/c.3 lineages plus TM0820 (e.22.1.2) and NamA (c.1.4.1) search hits against the bundle, with explicit limits on what was not retrieved. Reasoning: divergence within superfamily from combined evidence, multiple folds compatible with convergence or eroded ancient divergence, SCOPe makes no positive homology assertion across folds and that is not proof of analogy, convergence claim requires alignment/motif/phylogenetic evidence. Fold-not-homology and transfer limits covered.

Correct 2.04 different folds and superfamilies (b.23.2 vs b.18.1) and 2.08 shared fold/superfamily with distinct families b.18.1.36 vs b.18.1.3; correct SUNIDs. Explicitly notes different folds is not proof of unrelatedness, calls it structure-discovered remote homology, and bars function transfer. All criteria met.

All lineage, TaxId, sunids, boundaries, comments, hf definition/scope, and homology-endpoint claims are in the bundle. Homology retained; hf correctly read as a conformation statement not a sequence-relationship statement; fold-level a.4 description not assumed for d1ztra1; template and fold-level benchmark exclusion/separate handling, mutant and ligand caveats for both, no function transfer; states coordinates, quality data, and literature were not retrieved. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge, 2026-10-22.

Meets all criteria. Correctly places fr in heterogeneity/inconsistency rather than homology warnings, homology retained. Alignment restricted to present residues, missing elements as absent data. Representative: avoid fragment when complete domain exists; declines quality ranking without retrieved quality records and notes quality is not homology. Diversity: fragment counts for protein coverage but not structural variant; sensitivity analysis. Rejects function transfer. All facts supported by bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.

Correct recommendation; family asserts probable ancestry plus closer relationship and cannot be justified by fold match alone; new superfamily is an asymmetric withholding of a homology claim, not an analogy/convergence claim, revisable with intermediates/profiles/functional data; new fold needs core element/strand-order/connectivity difference, not decorations; denies function/template transfer; hits are evidence not classification. No fabricated identifiers. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Correct 2.08 hierarchy and sunids for d.144.1, d.144, class d and the three families, supported by the bundle. Separates fold similarity from the superfamily ancestry claim, draws a cautious shared phosphotransfer architecture inference, and explicitly refuses substrate (protein/aminoglycoside/lipid) and regulation transfer. Evidence list covers target family/domain assignment, active-site alignment, biochemistry, complex structures, non-catalytic regulatory domains and orthology. Complete. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.
